neighbours.label: news from an absent loved one: the moment a worried family member hears from, or is reassured by, a child or relative (heard from their child, reassure her that she was safe); ordinary 'from' a place or shop stays low
fire: His mother cried with relief when she finally heard from him in Paris.
They had not heard from their son since the earthquake struck.
He phoned his father to reassure him that the flight had landed.
The family waited for weeks to hear from the missing climber.
She sent her parents a text to reassure them that she was fine.
No one had heard from the fishing crew since Tuesday night.
Grandma was anxious until she heard from her grandson at college.
He wrote home to reassure his wife that the unit was safe.
quiet: His mother bought fresh bread when she finally reached the shop in Paris.
They had not bought anything from the store since the sale ended.
He phoned the hotel to ask whether the pool was open.
The family waited for weeks for the new sofa to be delivered.
She sent her parents a photo of the garden she had planted.
No one had ordered fish from the market since Tuesday night.
Grandma was busy until she finished knitting the blue scarf.
He wrote a report to explain how the new machine worked.

short: hearing from / reassuring a worried relative
notes: Card: 'rescue call comes from the child', 'reassure her that he's alright', 'heard her daughter's scream', 'heard from the Edmund Fitzgerald', ' from' x6.
